**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (e.g. your name, school, parentage etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **f)** Tell a story which illustrates the proverb: Health is better than wealth.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: a rich businessman who thinks money is everything.
2. He ignores his wife's and his doctor's advice.
3. Climax: a stroke, then the loss of his fortune on treatment.
4. Contrast with a poor but healthy neighbour.
5. Conclusion: the proverb stated as the lesson.

**Model composition (494 words)**

Mr Ebot was the richest businessman in our town. He owned three big shops, two lorries and a large house guarded by two dogs. He woke up before dawn every day and returned home late at night, and he often said to anyone who cared to listen, "Money is everything. A man with money fears nothing."

His wife, Mama Ruth, begged him many times to rest. "You have not seen a doctor for five years," she would say, "and you have been coughing for months." Mr Ebot only laughed. He ate whatever was quick, skipped meals during busy days, drank too many sugary drinks and slept only four hours a night. His doctor friend, Dr Neba, once advised him to take a holiday and to eat vegetables, but Mr Ebot answered, "I have no time to be sick."

One Monday morning, while he was counting money in his main shop, he felt a sharp pain in his chest. The room began to turn, and he fell to the floor. His workers rushed him to the hospital, where the doctors told his family that he had suffered a stroke caused by stress, overwork and poor feeding.

When Mr Ebot woke up, he could not move the right side of his body, and he could hardly speak. The doctors said that he needed expensive treatment abroad. His family sold one lorry and two plots of land to pay for the trip. For a year, he travelled between hospitals, spending money on operations, drugs and physiotherapy. The shops he had once supervised so closely began to fail because he was no longer there to manage them, and dishonest workers stole from the stock. Within two years, he had sold nearly everything he owned.

All this time, Mr Ebot's neighbour, Papa Tangem, a poor farmer, worked on his small farm each day. He ate vegetables, fruits and cassava from his garden, walked long distances every morning, and slept peacefully at night. He was not rich, but he was strong, cheerful and always singing. One evening, he visited Mr Ebot, who was sitting in front of the house in a wheelchair, and the two old men talked.

"Papa Tangem," said Mr Ebot with tears in his eyes, "I owned so much, but I would give all of it to walk as you walk, to eat as you eat and to sleep as you sleep. I worked so hard for wealth that I forgot to take care of the body that had to enjoy it."

Slowly, with the help of exercise and a healthy diet, Mr Ebot improved, though he never regained his old strength. He rebuilt a small business, closed his shop early every day and took time for his family and his health. Whenever young people visited him, he told them his story and ended with the same words: "Wealth can be earned again, but health once lost is hard to recover. Remember, health is better than wealth."

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing an essay about health and wealth instead of a story with characters and events.
2. A story that does not clearly illustrate the proverb, for example one in which the rich man loses money but his health plays no part.
